items.bold: BRENT SURGED PAST $126 (four-year high) — CENTCOM briefing Trump on new military options. Axios confirmed.
items.text: The Week (5 hours ago) confirmed: Brent crude surged past $126 per barrel — highest in four years — shattering optimism from earlier in the week. The trigger was an Axios report that CENTCOM was set to brief President Trump on new military options against Iran. The Week: "When the US-Israel coalition attacked Iran in late February, nine weeks ago, Brent was trading around $70 per barrel. It is now at $126, an 80% surge in under three months, driven almost entirely by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz." Business Standard confirmed: Brent surged as "reports said that the US has rejected Iran's peace proposal and directed to intensify the blockade at the Strait of Hormuz." This is the most significant single-day oil price trigger of the war — resumed US strikes now explicitly on the table for the first time since the ceasefire.

The toll system is now confirmed as operational, established, and being formalised into Iranian law. The IRGC Navy confirmed: any military vessel approaching the strait without coordination = ceasefire violation = "severe response."

assessment.body:
Thursday 5:30 PM IST. Day 62. The West Asia War's most dangerous day since February 28.

BRENT $126 — THE TRIGGER
• Axios: CENTCOM briefing Trump on new military options against Iran
• US rejected Iran's peace proposal (reopen Hormuz, defer nuclear)
• US directed intensification of the Hormuz blockade
• Brent surged from $111 open to $126 intraday — $15 surge in hours
• 80% above pre-war level of $70
• Four-year high. Highest since 2022 oil price peak

THE MILITARY OPTIONS MOMENT
• CENTCOM presented Trump with options: increase presence vs more aggressive operations
• Trump has not yet made a decision — expected additional Iran meetings
• If Trump approves new strikes: war enters most dangerous phase since Feb 28
• Brent could spike to $140-150 in a session on new strike announcement
• Nuclear sites (Fordow — only 30% damaged — greatest proliferation risk) could be targeted
• Iran has already revised its military doctrine to offensive

THE HORMUZ TOLL SYSTEM — NOW FORMALISED
• Iran's channel: north of Larak Island (not the main international lane)
• $2 million per ship confirmed — one ship paid this amount
• Pakistani tanker crossed March 16 with Iranian permission — first toll transit
• Idemitsu Maru (Japan) April 29 — second confirmed
• Iran Parliament formalising as law: hostile nations banned, others pay tolls + coordinate
• The toll is no longer a negotiating position — it is operational and becoming law

INDIA'S WORST DAY OF THE WAR
• Brent $126 = OMC hike Rs 12-18/L — most severe consumer shock since COVID
• Rupee Rs 95 — first breach of this level in the war. RBI intervention expected
• Sensex intraday -1,237. Nifty intraday -380. Partial recovery into close
• Kharif fertiliser: $2M/ship Hormuz toll = Gulf fertiliser commercially impossible
• Emergency alternate sourcing needed NOW: North Africa, Eastern Europe, Russia
• IndiGo among top losers — aviation sector in severe ATF cost crisis
• If CENTCOM military options approved: Brent $140-150, Sensex below 72,000

VERDICT: April 30 is Day 62 and the economic peak of the war for India. Brent at $126, rupee at Rs 95, Sensex intraday down 1,237 points, CENTCOM presenting Trump with military strike options against Iran. The West Asia War is no longer in a stalemate. It is approaching a binary decision point: a nuclear deal that ends the blockade (Brent $80, Sensex 87,000+) or a resumption of military strikes (Brent $150, Sensex 52,000). India is paying the highest price of any non-combatant nation in this war. And the decision that determines India's economic fate for the rest of 2026 is being made in the White House Situation Room — not in New Delhi.
